title: QCAT mobility analyzer
subtitle: Find the evidence behind a handover
summary: Reconstruct LTE and UMTS mobility from large QCAT text exports, tracing each procedure back to its measurement configuration, target cell, and outcome.
problem: A handover message tells you what happened. Explaining why requires the measurement configuration that was active at that moment, including changes across split captures.
built: I built a two-pass Python pipeline: extract relevant records once, then reconstruct mobility procedures from the smaller event stream. Split capture parts are treated as a continuous session so earlier measurement configurations remain available.
decision: Resolve each measurement report against the configuration at its timestamp. Accept a report as a handover trigger only when it names the commanded target cell. Preserve the difference between a reported signal bin and a configured threshold.
result: Produces a self-contained HTML report, an event CSV, and structured JSON. Each mobility event can be investigated through its trigger, cells, measurement gaps, stage timing, and outcome.
limit: LTE and UMTS mobility are supported. GSM records are extracted but are not yet analyzed. The diagram below describes the pipeline; it contains no customer captures.
discussion: How do you avoid a plausible but incorrect attribution when measurement IDs are reused?

title: DTLog
subtitle: Turn captures into defensible campaign KPIs
summary: Decode SCAT-format UE captures, reconstruct signaling procedures, and pool coverage, mobility, accessibility, and voice evidence across a drive-test campaign.
problem: A capture contains repeated messages, incomplete procedures, and unreadable outcomes. Counting messages or averaging per-log percentages can produce confident but misleading network KPIs.
built: I built a decoder and procedure-analysis engine with retransmission deduplication, state-machine detection, decoded cause codes, and a FastAPI / React dashboard. Campaign results are also available as Excel reports.
decision: Give each signaling event one procedure owner. Pool KPI numerators and denominators before calculating rates. Keep indeterminate outcomes separate from observed failures, and show counts when samples are too small for a useful percentage.
result: Connects campaign-level findings to individual procedures and their evidence. Decode caching supports repeated analysis without dissecting the same capture every time.
limit: NR frames can be decoded, but NR procedure segmentation is not implemented. Missing radio metrics are reported as unavailable rather than estimated. Source and capture sets are private.
discussion: When does a missing completion message represent a failed procedure, and when is the capture inconclusive?
access: Private repository · case study available here

title: Site Insights
subtitle: Make radio configuration relationships reviewable
summary: Transform Nokia SCF / XML configurations into LTE and NR inventories, mobility relation matrices, carrier-aggregation checks, and snapshot comparisons.
problem: A configured neighbor does not guarantee a usable mobility path. Feature flags, measurements, target dependencies, and cell relationships need to be checked together.
built: I independently developed configuration-analysis automation for weekly LTE / NR inventories and repeatable lab reviews. The tools inspect intra-frequency, inter-frequency, and inter-RAT mobility, reselection, redirection, and carrier aggregation.
decision: Separate successful paths from blocked or incomplete configurations. Preserve the reasons behind each decision, and compare both XML snapshots and generated inventories to expose changes.
result: Generates client and internal relation workbooks and identifies added, removed, and changed parameters and relationships. An offline Windows package supports environments without a Python installation or runtime internet access.
limit: Configuration eligibility is evidence about the configured network, not proof that a handover succeeds over the air. Customer configurations and outputs are excluded from this portfolio.
discussion: How do you separate a configuration that looks complete from a mobility path that is actually eligible?

title: Cellular Analyzer
subtitle: Put radio measurements on the route
summary: Collect device-exposed LTE / NR measurements with GPS location, retain drive-test sessions, and export measurements for coverage analysis.
problem: Radio measurements are more useful when they can be connected to where the device was and what it was doing, rather than read as isolated signal values.
built: I developed an Android application using telephony APIs to collect available RSRP, RSRQ, SINR, PCI, cell identity, and frequency information alongside GPS location. Foreground-service logging supports measurement collection with the screen off.
decision: Use device-exposed measurements and keep availability explicit. Local session storage and CSV export make measurements portable for later analysis instead of tying the data to one view.
result: Combines route visualization, measurement logging, and export in a field-oriented application. The measurement stream can be correlated with drive-test routes during post-test coverage review.
limit: Android measurement availability depends on the device, modem, and OS version. Device-exposed metrics do not replace a dedicated RF measurement instrument. The repository is private.
discussion: How do you design a useful measurement tool when modem and OS access vary by device?
access: Private repository · case study available here

title: LTE KPI clustering
subtitle: Find coverage regions in the measurement data
summary: Apply K-means to LTE RSRP, RSRQ, and throughput data to identify heterogeneous coverage regions and cell-edge performance gaps.
problem: A network-wide average can hide local coverage and performance differences. Measurement groups can help reveal regions that deserve a closer RF investigation.
built: I applied K-means clustering to LTE signal and throughput measurements and visualized the resulting coverage regions. The repository includes the notebook, Python implementation, and cluster-map outputs.
decision: Use clustering as an exploratory tool. Interpret clusters against the underlying radio measurements rather than treating a cluster label as a network fault diagnosis.
result: Identified coverage and cell-edge performance gaps and used them to recommend parameter changes in a proof of concept.
limit: This is an exploratory proof of concept. Its findings depend on the dataset and feature selection and should be validated through additional measurements before deployment.
discussion: How do you translate an unsupervised cluster into a testable RF optimization hypothesis?

title: CNN QAM denoiser
subtitle: Explore learned denoising for communication signals
summary: Investigate convolutional neural networks for denoising QAM-modulated audio signals, connecting signal-processing concepts with machine learning.
problem: Noise degrades communication signals. This project explores whether a learned denoising approach can help recover information from QAM-modulated audio.
built: I explored a convolutional neural network approach to QAM signal denoising. The public repository documents the project as a deep-learning investigation into communication clarity.
decision: Frame learned denoising as an experiment whose value depends on evaluation across noise conditions and against conventional baselines.
result: A research project at the intersection of communications and machine learning, complementing my later work on measurement and validation tools.
limit: The public project summary does not establish a production deployment or a quantified performance advantage. No benchmark result is claimed here.
discussion: What baselines and noise conditions would you use to establish whether a learned denoiser generalizes?
